headline: High: shared filesystem and broad write/network defaults create medium-to-high risks of leakage, conflicts, and cascading errors between Cline and gpt-engineer.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cline can read/write workspace files and use MCP, while gpt-engineer writes files in the project directory and can execute generated code. That shared filesystem bridge means one agent can place instruction-like content for the other to ingest. No direct browser-to-browser or clipboard bridge is shown, so medium fits better than high.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace or project directory, injected instructions can cross from one agent to the other.
IF either agent parses file contents as trusted instructions, prompt injection becomes actionable.
mitigations: Separate the agents into different directories.
Disable MCP for Cline when processing untrusted files.
Review generated files before the other agent reads them.
Use a human approval step for any file that contains instructions or prompts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents have filesystem read access and broad network egress, and Cline explicitly touches source code and browser screenshots while gpt-engineer touches generated source code. In a shared workspace, sensitive code or screenshots can flow from one agent into the other and then out through model/API calls. The pair is not local-only, so leakage risk is above low.
conditions: IF the two agents share a project directory, files readable by one can be exposed to the other.
IF either agent sends file contents to its configured model backend, workspace data can leave the local environment.
mitigations: Keep sensitive files outside the shared project directory.
Use separate API keys and model endpoints per agent.
Turn off network access for one agent during sensitive edits.
Redact screenshots and secrets before either agent reads them.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write the same filesystem and spawn subprocesses; Cline also modifies git state, while gpt-engineer writes files in the project directory. With shared-state-by-filesystem/project-directory concurrency and no locking shown, concurrent edits can overwrite each other or corrupt git state. The overlap is dangerous by default and can cause irreversible repository damage.
conditions: IF both agents run against the same repository or project directory, concurrent writes can collide.
IF Cline modifies git state while gpt-engineer writes files, repository history or working tree state can diverge.
mitigations: Run only one agent at a time on a given repo.
Use separate branches for each agent.
Add a manual diff review before any git commit.
Snapshot the workspace before concurrent experimentation.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cline can produce browser-derived or code-derived outputs, and gpt-engineer is designed to write files from prompts and then offer to run them. That makes A’s output a likely input to B without a verification gate, so mistakes or hallucinations can cascade into generated code or executed actions. The blast radius includes broken code and unsafe commands.
conditions: IF gpt-engineer consumes Cline-produced text as authoritative, errors can propagate into generated code.
IF the generated code is then executed with the user's privileges, the cascade can become operationally harmful.
mitigations: Insert a human verification step between agents.
Require citations or diffs before gpt-engineer acts on Cline output.
Disable auto-run of generated code.
Limit Cline to producing summaries, not executable instructions.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source coding agents with no explicit residency, certification, or retention claims, so a concrete compliance mismatch is not established. The only clear issue is that Cline handles browser screenshots and source code while gpt-engineer handles generated source code, which could matter if regulated data is placed in the shared workspace. Because the mismatch is not documented, low is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in the shared workspace, both agents may process it without documented controls.
IF one deployment requires stricter retention than the other, the mismatch becomes operational.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared project directory.
Use a separate workspace for compliance-sensitive work.
Document retention and deletion handling before use.
Avoid screenshots containing personal or regulated data.
